analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md. The changed hunk replaces the manual "Updating Darkbloom on the pair" procedure (base lines 536-562) with a description of automatic pair updates (head 536-583, plus a small edit near 644-645). The supplied head text stops at line 455 and the patch excerpt is cut off after the first new list item. The remaining head content for the changed region was therefore not visible, and no finding can cite a visible head line. The visible new text says each Mac's cluster service asks the coordinator for its latest release every 30 minutes at a slot derived from the cluster ID, then downloads, verifies and stages it. It also gates this on auto_update and DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK. The rest of the document (pairing, model copy over the encrypted link, approvals, local-only API, prefix cache) is unchanged in the supplied ranges. It stays consistent with T-041 (per-tenant cache scope, encrypted SSD tier, 30-minute TTL) and with the existing statements about the cable-link encryption contract and the approval checks. Because this is documentation, no security control in code changes within the evidence. The open question for later review is the unseen code behind the documented behavior. Does the automatic update path use the same signed-artifact verification, A-011 binary-hash and A-017 qualification checks as the single-Mac updater? How does it handle rollback and the watchdog (T-043)? Do both Macs apply a coordinated restart without breaking the shared approval or key binding? Is there any downgrade protection? The threat model has no entry for the pair auto-update flow, so its TB-002/TB-003/T-043 text may need an update once the complete section and the implementing code are reviewed.
